headline: Apple's Private Relay could reveal your IP address to websites
summary: Researchers found a WebKit issue that may expose user IPs when using passkeys on Safari and other iOS browsers.
details: Security researchers have discovered a flaw in Apple's Private Relay feature, which is designed to mask user IP addresses. A WebKit issue means that websites and services could potentially see your IP address, undermining the privacy promised by the iCloud+ feature.

The vulnerability is particularly concerning when using passkeys for password-free logins. When a passkey authentication request is made outside of Safari, Private Relay, which is tied to the browser, does not provide full device protection like a VPN. This can lead to IP address leaks.

The problem extends beyond Safari, as the underlying WebKit engine is used by all browsers on iOS. This means that even privacy-focused browsers like OnionBrowser and Psylo could be affected, potentially exposing user IPs when passkeys are utilized.

The researchers have alerted the Tor Project and OnionBrowser developers, sharing potential solutions. Apple has acknowledged the report and stated it is investigating the issue. However, past experiences, like the year-long delay in fixing an iCloud Hide My Email leak, suggest a resolution might take considerable time.
